recap.workouts: Week one of the hybrid program opened with a full Monday. Legs A went in first, before class: belt squat 2 x 10 at 110 lb (top of the range on both sets), leg extension 2 x 12 at 115 lb, seated leg curl 4 x 12 at 60 lb (top of the range on all four), tibialis raise 20 lb for 16 reps on the first set and the second set logged without reps. Then the class, logged as an 88-minute session: average HR 137, max 184, load 74, and you rated it a 9 (the lifting a 6). You wrote that you went hard and held the bar to 135 lb because your legs were already spent from the gym work, which is a sound way to make that order work. It was a Workout activity, so there is no rep-by-rep deep-dive for it, by design. The club run was not in the 18:30 data, so I have nothing to report on it tonight; if you get out for it or the easy spin, tomorrow's fetch will pick it up.
recap.takeaways: 1) Legs A was a clean opening deposit. Belt squat hit 10 on both sets and the leg curl hit 12 on all four, so both earn their next step from the plan (belt squat to 120, leg curl to 65). Leg extension went at 115 rather than the 120 the plan wrote, and 12 and 12 is inside the 10-15 range, so it simply stands where it is. 2) Nine out of ten for the class after a leg session is a big day, and it was earned; the 135 lb call kept it honest. Nothing to fix, just let tomorrow be the easy day it is built to be. 3) Nothing has been changed in the week: the club run was an easy session with an amber option, either version counts, and nothing is owed if it does not happen.
recap.tomorrow: Tomorrow: the class is 'Occipital' (5 rounds with 400 m runs, muscle-ups, 500 m row and box jumps; your call on scaling), then Upper 1, push plus triceps, about 30 minutes: incline DB press 3 x 8-12 at 70 lb, cable fly 2 x 12-15 at 45 lb, lateral raise 3 x 15-20 at 20 lb, triceps pushdown 3 x 8-12 at 110 lb. The afternoon ride is CF9, at least 6 hours after class, 45-75 minutes under the Zone 2 ceiling (190 W) with the 10 minutes at 165 W at minutes 20-30, which never move. Green: Zwift or outside, steady, or 5 x 1 minute high-cadence spin-ups if you feel sharp. Amber: CF6, 45 minutes, all easy, the 165 W block still in. If your legs are fresh and the warm-up rolls by minute ten, that says green; if the legs are heavy after today, amber. The morning dashboard makes the call from readiness, and you can take either; both are a good day's work.

recapPrev.workouts:
CrossFit was Maple, the chipper: 60 cal echo bike, 20-inch step-ups, a 20 lb med-ball piece, 30 burpees, and 19 muscle-ups in place of the class's strict pull-ups, time-capped at 18 minutes. RPE 5 - a controlled effort, and the echo bike went closer to the men's TRAIN pace (60 cal) than the FITNESS scale the plan actually called for (50 cal). Hypertrophy was the pull + triceps + leg-maintenance day: lat pulldown 210x12/12, barbell row 85x8/9, face pull 95x15/16, barbell curl 65x10/10, overhead triceps extension 150x12 then a swap to French press at 45x12 for the second set, belt squats subbed for leg curls at 110x12, tibia raise 20x20/15. RPE 5. Nothing sore or flagged in your notes today.

Then the retest: CT31, moved here from Monday as you asked. Total time 60:05, and the 24-minute Zone 3 tune block held very steady - 224 W average, only 0.5% variation second to second, about as clean a pacing job as this block gets. Compliance came in at 110% of the planned load. Heart rate told a slightly different story: it settled at 161 for the block, two beats above the 159 bike LTHR that band was tested against, with a modest 4.2 bpm of drift over the 24 minutes and 3.2% decoupling - well inside the coupled range, so nothing like a blow-up, just running a shade hot at that output. tune.py read it as threshold likely down a touch (or just a harder day) and took the conservative nudge rather than a bigger correction - more in the takeaways below. One thing worth naming as a hypothesis and not a finding: this morning's Maple went a notch harder than the FITNESS call written for it (the higher echo-bike pace, muscle-ups for pull-ups), and while that call was written with a run in mind for this afternoon rather than the bike session that actually landed here, a few hours of residual load from a harder morning is a plausible, unprovable piece of why HR ran warm on the block. Tonight's automated deep-dive file for this ride hadn't generated by the time this recap ran, so this read comes from tune.py's own per-second analysis of the block rather than the full rep-by-rep stream report - a gap on the pipeline side, not in your effort.
recapPrev.takeaways:
Bike anchors moved for the first time since July: FTP 236 to 229 watts, bike LTHR unchanged at 159, run anchors untouched. This was a conservative nudge (confidence medium), not a big correction - HR sat two beats above LTHR at a very cleanly paced output, but drift and decoupling both stayed in the normal range. Worth watching whether the next tune confirms it or today was just a harder day.

Live hypothesis, not a verdict: an ambitious Maple this morning - Train-pace bike, muscle-ups - landing a few hours before the retest may have contributed to the warmer HR. Can't prove it from one day's data, but it's a pattern worth tracking if it shows up again.

No changes to the rest of the week - CrossFit, hypertrophy and the retest all landed as planned, nothing to absorb or reschedule.
recapPrev.tomorrow:
Wednesday is CrossFit only - travel day, no hypertrophy, no endurance. Save the legs and lungs for Thursday's full rest day. The class is a Clean & Jerk single build plus the metcon Oak: 15-12-9 deadlifts and jump-rope singles. Check the grip and the first pull off the floor on the warm-up, and how the legs feel walking into 36 deadlifts.

Barbell feeling good, ready to move? Build the clean and jerk briskly toward a strong, confident single - not a max hunt, that's off the table for the whole week regardless - and let Oak's deadlifts move with purpose.

Legs flat, everything feeling heavy? Keep the ladder light and technical, and let Oak's reps land at an easier, unhurried pace.

Both are a good day's work; this is a one-job travel day, not one to make or break.

sys: CORRECTION, same rerun: Sascha flagged that the sleeping-HR figure (90) did not match his own iOS Health app. He then ran the export manually and asked whether it was evaluating the wrong timeframe — very likely yes. The email's sleep-STAGE segments (individually dated, reliable) showed it had bundled TWO nights, evidence that this export's query window was not cleanly scoped to one night; the five header summary figures (HR avg/min, resp rate, wrist temp, and the fifth field logged silently) carry no per-night date stamp at all, so once one of them is shown wrong there is no way to trust the others were scoped correctly either — 90 vs a 63 baseline, with a same-night min of 62, is also just a very wide spread for one night, consistent with daytime samples leaking into the average. RESOLUTION: pulled all five header-derived fields from the 2026-09-28 sleep_nightly_2026.csv row, keeping only the timing (20:34→05:24, 8.83 h total, 8.50 h asleep) which comes from the individually-dated sleep-stage segments themselves and isn't affected by this failure mode. Re-ran readiness.py --today 2026-09-28 on the corrected row: valid true (its 3-night HR/RR smoothing still has 2026-09-21 and 2026-09-22 to fall back on, so it did not need to refuse), asOf 2026-09-28, asOfIsToday true, daysBehind 0, readinessIndex 37, status under — driven by the last known-good nights, not by the bad number. AMBER pick on today's RF6 unchanged. Told Sascha plainly what was wrong, why, what was corrected, and asked him to share his Health app's actual sleeping-HR figure so it can be logged properly rather than left blank. Everything else from this morning stands: pipeline all ok:true, no hygiene deletions this fetch, program.py/progression.py --check both passed, plan manifest matches, phone-sync still unsynced since 2026-09-25T17:57Z. Zones unchanged: FTP 229 W, bike LTHR 159, run TP 262 s/km, run LTHR 167. Self-scanned every rendered field for the publish guard's patterns before writing — 0 blocking (2 pre-existing advisory decoupling mentions remain untouched in recapPrev). Nothing here implies underfueling; no standing body-part caveat.
